title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A concrete worked example shows how a model's selections from a mixed question bank are scored to measure rule violations.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, gray arrows, red annotations on flagged items
description: Three boxed panels run left to right, joined by gray arrows. The left panel, headed 'User', holds a prompt in which the LLM plays a hiring manager. The prompt gives a job (Construction Painter) and a bank of 200 interview questions, and asks for exactly 25 to be selected. The middle panel, headed 'Assistant', lists selected questions as rows. Lawful questions have green backgrounds. Two unlawful ones have salmon backgrounds, such as 'What is your nationality?' and 'What days do you worship?'. Orange arrows and small red italic notes point to these two rows and name the Title VII ground. The right panel, headed 'Illegal Selection Rate (ISR)', shows the formula: unlawful selected questions divided by total selected questions, 2/25 = 8%. Captions sit under each panel. The eye goes first to the colored rows in the middle.
caption: HireWatch illustrative evaluation example. The LLM hiring assistant receives a job description plus additional hiring-relevant context and is instructed to select 25 questions from a 200-item bank. Each item in this bank has been pre-labeled as lawful or unlawful under federal employment discrimination law. We report Illegal Selection Rate (ISR), the fraction of selections drawn from the unlawful set (in this example, 2 of 25 selections are unlawful, ISR = 8%). HireWatch evaluates 18 closed and open-source LLMs across 7 contextual escalation tiers and 4 legal compliance instructions.
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. We instruct LLMs to select questions from this bank in preparing for job interviews, across a set of various occupations and contexts, and report the fraction of unlawful questions that LLMs select. Evaluation of 18 closed and open-weight LLMs across ~100,000 trials under different types of contextual pressure reveals that LLMs' legal compliance is brittle. While LLMs generally avoid selecting unlawful questions in low-pressure contexts, legal violations increase sharply under higher pressure. Explicit prompts to comply with law can improve compliance rates, but do not altogether eliminate legal violations. We publicly release our code and data at https://github.com/hnghiem-nlp/hirewatch_repo.
